questions.questionText:
In economics, natural sunlight is classified as a free good.
What is the reason for this?

options.text: Sunlight is a gift of nature.
Sunlight is a renewable resource.
There is no opportunity cost of using sunlight.
Unlimited amounts of sunlight can be consumed.

questions.questionText: What would be classified as the factor of production capital for an airline?

options.text: the aircraft operated by the airline
the money the airline keeps in the bank
the pilots the airline uses
the shares of the airline quoted on the stock market

questions.questionText: What is a major advantage of a market economic system over a mixed economic system?

options.text: All production of goods and services is determined by consumer demand.
Ownership of resources is divided between private and public sectors.
Producers include any external costs they create in the price of the good.
There will always be an even distribution of income and wealth.

questions.questionText: What does a commercial bank not provide?

options.text: cash
bonds
loans
mortgages

questions.questionText: What will be likely to increase the wages of airline pilots?

options.text: Incomes increase in the world’s major economies.
Terrorist attacks decrease tourist travel.
The cost of aviation fuel rises.
The world economy goes into recession.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to help a trade union’s claim for wage increases in an industry?

options.text: a decrease in the price of a close substitute for the product
a decrease in the qualifications needed for the job
an increase in the number of workers
an increase in the profits of the industry

questions.questionText: What is a characteristic of a perfectly competitive firm?

options.text: absence of competitors
non-price competition
one dominant firm
price taker

questions.questionText: What is a possible cause of diseconomies of scale?

options.text: an increase in extra administration
an increase in raw materials costs
an increase in taxation on company profits
an increase in the national minimum wage

questions.questionText:
A firm that sells its product for $6 a unit has the following total costs.
output (units) 0 10 20 30
total costs ($) 40 100 120 150
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Average cost is lowest when 10 units are produced.
The firm does not make any profit when 20 units are sold.
The firm has no fixed costs.
Total variable costs fall continuously over these outputs.

questions.questionText: Which statement about fixed costs is correct?

options.text: They exist only in the long run.
They include raw material and direct labour costs.
They increase at the same rate as output.
They must be paid even if there is no output.

questions.questionText: Which is a supply-side policy?

options.text: increasing interest rates
increasing taxation
providing training courses
selling government bonds

questions.questionText: What is an aim of government policy?

options.text: income tax
interest rates
stable prices
unemployment

questions.questionText:
Which situation involving the building industry is most likely to be investigated by a government
body set up to control restrictive practices?

options.text: a builder purchasing a plot of land for development of housing
groups of suppliers of building materials agreeing to fix prices
several builders bidding for the same contracts
several builders using different sources of supply

questions.questionText:
The table shows the change in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of four countries.
Which country has experienced a recession?
quarterly percentage change in GDP
Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4
% % % %
What determines the weights in the consumer prices index (CPI)?

options.text: the average income received by the various households
the average increase in the prices of the different goods
the proportion of income spent by the average household on particular goods
the proportion of income that the average household saves

questions.questionText:
There was a fall in investment spending by businesses in the third quarter of 2015.
What would be the likely result of this?

options.text: an increase in economic growth
an increase in exports
an increase in incomes
an increase in unemployment

questions.questionText:
The table shows units of output, value of output and number of people employed in an industry
over three years.
output output value number employed
(units, millions) ($ millions) (000)
year 1 10 10 5
year 2 21 25 7
year 3 32 40 8
What can be concluded from the table?

options.text: Inflation has increased.
Productivity has increased.
Profit has increased.
Working population has increased.

questions.questionText: Which feature is found in a developed country rather than a developing country?

options.text: high levels of rural to urban migration
highly organised international financial markets
low proportion of workforce in service industries
low school-leaving age

questions.questionText:
Over two-thirds of the world’s poorest people live in rural areas. They are mainly involved in
subsistence agriculture.
What explains why poverty remains at a high level for subsistence farming families?

options.text: a lack of finance to buy machinery to improve productivity
low international prices for food due to overproduction
the size of families is too small to work the land
women are discouraged from doing agricultural work

questions.questionText:
The government of a developing country allows a multinational mining company to mine minerals
in order to improve the standard of living of the local people.
Which action by the multinational company (MNC) will not lead to an improvement in the
standard of living of the local people?

options.text: building roads to assist transport
exporting mineral ore
providing skills training
returning profits overseas

questions.questionText:
A country wishes to follow a policy of trade protection.
Which action would it take?

options.text: increase the level of import quotas
reduce import tariffs
remove exchange controls
subsidise export producers

questions.questionText:
In 2012 the UK held the Olympic Games, which attracted a large number of visitors from foreign
countries.
Which item of the UK’s current account balance will have benefited directly from this event?

options.text: export trade in goods
export trade in services
import trade in goods
import trade in services

questions.questionText:
In 2015, the value of the South African currency (the rand) depreciated against the US dollar.
What effect did this have on the US economy?

options.text: Exports to South Africa became more expensive.
The current account deficit of the US decreased.
The US experienced higher levels of inflation.
Unemployment in the US decreased.

questions.questionText:
The table shows the rice yield in four countries.
rice yield
country
(kilos per hectare)
Japan 64
China 53
Bangladesh 20
Thailand 20
What may be concluded from this information?

options.text: Bangladesh and Thailand produce the same amount of rice.
Japan produces more than three times as much rice as Bangladesh.
Japan produces the largest amount of rice per hectare.

Japan produces the largest amount of rice per person employed.
